source.title: Data from: Mob and rotational grazing influence pasture biomass, nutritive value, and species composition
source.access: public; anonymous version ZIP download returned HTTP 200 without credentials
source.license: CC0 1.0, as declared by the Dryad public API

population.ageOrPhysiologicalClass: not applicable to the reported forage observations; study pasture was grazed by yearling beef cattle
population.location: Hawbecker Research Farm, northeastern United States
population.system: four-year mob versus rotational grazing comparison, 2015-2018
population.unitOfObservation: plot-level forage sample nested within treatment, replicate/paddock, year, and harvest time
population.repeatedMeasures: same eight treatment x replicate paddocks over multiple years and harvest times; retain paddock grouping

measurement.dryMatterInterpretation: study and article describe dry matter mass; the source column header itself says kg/ha
measurement.targetMethod: published methods describe ten 0.1 m2 pre-grazing quadrat clippings per paddock to 2.5 cm, averaged to paddock mean
measurement.predictor: mean pre-grazing sward height at paddock/replicate level
measurement.sourcePredictorGranularity: paddock/replicate mean; not point-matched to each biomass quadrat
measurement.outcomeGrainAfterAggregation: treatment x replicate/paddock x study year x Julian day

eligibility.technicalAvailability: ELIGIBLE; complete public archive obtained and internal file checksums verified
eligibility.zootechnicalCompatibility: CONDITIONAL for a separate pasture forage biomass module; not an animal intake or performance cohort
eligibility.statisticalSufficiency: CONDITIONAL; 64 repeated measurements across only eight paddocks, requiring group-preserving analysis
eligibleUses: separate external forage biomass evaluation after estimand and measurement-grain review
limitations: Height is paddock-level and biomass samples are plot-level; only the declared paddock-time aggregation aligns them.
Only eight paddock groups are available and they recur over time.
The study is a temperate northeastern-US grass-legume system and does not establish calibration for Brazilian tropical pastures.
The associated study did not collect animal performance outcomes.
